(1) comprehension is similar in the two media, but (2) readers of the Kindle are less efficient than readers of the print book in locating events in the space and in the temporality, and (3) readers of the print pocket book are less efficient in the beginning of the text, but they catch up later on.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of sensorimotor information in reading comprehension and suggests that it is not only the visual information that is important, but the kinesthetic feedback that is provided by the manipulation of a paper book.
the question of the role of the book as a physical object in reading.

the question of whether or not the reading experience is similar when reading in print and on a Kindle, and we have found that, basically it is, but the spatial and temporal organization of the text is less well understood with a Kindle than with a book.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reading on a Kindle is as efficient as in print book for the comprehension of a text, but the lack of kinesthetic feedback may be a handicap when the story is very long and complex.
, when reading long texts, a Kindle is a good alternative to a book, but, when the text is long enough to require several sessions, it is better to use a book.
the reading of a text on a Kindle is as efficient as reading in print, but the reader is less efficient at building a coherent spatial and temporal representation of the story.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when reading a text, readers are not only relying on the visual information provided by the words, but also on the spatial and tactile information provided by the manipulation of paper books.
the reading of a long story is basically a spatial and temporal process, and that, when the sensorimotor feedback is not available, readers have difficulties to organize events in space and time.
the reading medium has a limited impact on reading comprehension, but that it may affect the reader’s ability to build a correct representation of the story’s chronology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reading on an electronic device is not the same as reading in a book.
, although the reading experience is different on Kindle and in print, the comprehension is similar, at least for long texts.

reading on a digital device is as good as reading in a print pocketbook for the comprehension of the story, but that the lack of haptic feedback on a digital device may have a negative effect on the reader’s capacity to locate events in time and space.
